newsitem.title: USA: AMGEN FALLS ON LOWER SALES FORECAST.
newsitem.headline: AMGEN FALLS ON LOWER SALES FORECAST.

text.p: Amgen Inc said its stock fell sharply after it forecast lower-than-expected sales of its key Epogen drug in the second half of the year.

The forecast, contained in a 10-Q filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, said Epogen sales growth in the second half of the year would be less than 15 percent, a company spokeswoman said. This revises a forecast Amgen made a month ago saying Epogen sales would grow at about 15 percent in the second half. Amgen was down 4-3/16 to 52-15/16.
The company said the revised forecast reflects a delayed implementation of new Medicare reimbursement rules.
The new rules essentially make it more difficult for patients to qualify for reimbursement for Epogen, which boosts red blood cell count and is used by people undergoing kidney dialysis.

Amgen's spokeswoman said the implementation of these rules has been delayed twice, adding to the uncertainty over who will qualify for reimbursement as well as leading doctors to be extra cautious. The rules are now set to take effect September 1.

Amgen also said in its 10Q that total company sales for 1997 will grow somewhat less than 10 percent. In 1996, Epogen sales were up 21 percent, while sales of Amgen's other drug, Neupogen, were up nine percent.
